correctness.rationale: The maximal-minor determinant is exactly the ordinary Vandermonde product times the sum of the four column roots. Distinctness removes the Vandermonde factor. For four unit roots, zero sum also forces the third elementary symmetric function to vanish, so their monic quartic is even and the roots are two antipodal pairs. Antipodes occur among N-th roots exactly for even N. Counting pairs gives binomial(N/2,2), and the first three rows force rank exactly 3. An exact-integer checker independently verifies the determinant identity and all four-column subsets for 5<=N<=40.
